ENT Clinical Note – Telehealth Visit  
Clinician: Dr Smith  
Patient: Barbara [lastname not stated], DOB 04 Oct 1984  
Date: [today’s date not provided]

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure  
  • 3-day history of profuse diarrhoea and repetitive vomiting. No food, medication, or environmental trigger identified; likely infectious contact (brother with same illness).

- Symptom timeline and progression  
  • Onset: 3 days ago.  
  • Course: Initially watery stools, now very loose; ≥4 bowel movements today. Persistent vomiting of all oral intake including water and oral rehydration solution (ORS). Subjective high fever since onset. Abdominal pain peri-umbilical, colicky, precedes urge to defecate.

- ENT symptoms  
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denies.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Denies.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: Denies (vomiting related; no pain on swallowing).  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Denies.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing or dyspnea: Denies.  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: Denies.  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: Denies.  
  • Neck pain/swelling: Denies.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments  
  • No similar gastrointestinal episodes previously.  
  • Home management: ORS solution 3 ×/day for 2 days without improvement. No anti-diarrhoeals, anti-emetics, or antibiotics used. No prior emergency or hospital visits for current illness.

- Allergies and current medications  
  • Drug/food allergies: Not documented.  
  • Current meds: Vitamin D daily (dose/route not documented). Occasional ibuprofen for menstrual cramps (last taken not stated).

- Social context  
  • Lives with brother and mother; brother currently unwell with similar symptoms. Able to work from home; currently supervised at home.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported.  
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, dyspnea, or increased work of breathing reported.  
- Mental status: Appears alert and interactive via video.  
- Vitals and examination: Not recorded (remote visit); patient reports feeling “boiling hot.” Localised periumbilical tenderness on self-palpation.  
- Presence of another person: Brother and mother at home (not present on call).

Assessment:
- Working impression: Acute infectious gastroenteritis (viral most likely; bacterial possible). ENT/anaphylactic pathology not suspected – no airway or oropharyngeal involvement.

Evidence summary  
  • Sudden onset watery diarrhoea, vomiting, subjective fever.  
  • Household cluster with brother and wider school cohort.  
  • No blood in stool, no rash, no ENT or respiratory manifestations.

DDx (aligned with transcript)  
1. Acute viral gastroenteritis – highly likely: family cluster, classic symptom triad, typically self-limited.  
2. Acute bacterial gastroenteritis – moderate likelihood: persistent >72 h and subjective high fever; stool culture arranged.  
(Other DDx from system—food-borne toxin illness, IBD—considered much less likely; opposing evidence as above.)  
No ENT differential diagnoses applicable.  

Plan:
- Immediate/ongoing care  
  • Continue ORS; advise tiny frequent sips to maximize absorption and limit emesis.  
  • Simple diet (toast, biscuits); avoid milk, raw fruit/veg, alcohol.  

- Investigations  
  • Arrange urgent clinic appointment for stool sample collection and hydration assessment as discussed.  

- Escalation / red-flags  
  • Call EMS / attend A&E if: inability to keep fluids down with decreased urine output, persistent vomiting of bile or blood, severe abdominal pain, syncope, new fever ≥38.5 °C, or any breathing difficulty/airway swelling (none presently).  

- Follow-up  
  • Clinic appointment booking via support line (urgent).  
  • Telephone re-contact if symptoms worsen before scheduled visit.  
  • Consider GP/allergy follow-up only if new ENT or allergic manifestations develop (not currently indicated).  

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but expected:  
  – Objective vitals (temperature, HR, BP, RR, SpO₂).  
  – Complete allergy list.  
  – Documentation of current medication doses/routes.  
  – Verification of hydration status (mucous membranes, capillary refill, urine colour).  
  – ENT physical findings (oropharyngeal exam) not possible via phone.  
● Conflicts between transcript & DDx: None noted; both align on infectious gastroenteritis aetiology.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional minor audio gaps but clinical content preserved.
